subject: does "zeroinflatednbinomial1strata" allow fitting of regression models for the zero inflation probability of zero-inflated models?

messages.author: cffc1319a2f89155
messages.subject: does "zeroinflatednbinomial1strata" allow fitting of regression models for the zero inflation probability of zero-inflated models?
parts:
Dear all,

I have a question with regards to INLA's options for zero inflated models. 

In Arab (2015) I read the following sentence: "INLA does not allow fitting a regression model for the zero-inflation probability of the zero-inflated models". 

According to R there seems to be a set of new likelihood models named "zeroinflatednbinomial1strata" 1, 2 and 3. However, I cannot find any documentation for these likelihood models. I was wondering if any of these strata models does allow fitting of regression models for the zero-inflation probability of zero-inflated models? 

Thanks for your help.

Regards.

Robert



Arab (2015). Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Models for Modeling Epidemiological Data with Excess Zeros. 
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4586626/

> Dear all,
>
> I have a question with regards to INLA's options for zero inflated
> models. 
>
> In Arab (2015) I read the following sentence: "INLA does not allow
> fitting a regression model for the zero-inflation probability of the
> zero-inflated models". 
>
> According to R there seems to be a set of new likelihood models named
> "zeroinflatednbinomial1strata" 1, 2 and 3. However, I cannot find any
> documentation for these likelihood models. I was wondering if any of
> these strata models does allow fitting of regression models for the
> zero-inflation probability of zero-inflated models? 
>

Hi,

these are kind of special models made for a spesific purpose and not
ment to be of public use

if you look at inla.doc("zeroinf")

then for type0, then if the reponse is a 0, then you know which
component it is from. in these likelihoods, that probability is set to
'p', but you can also just set that one fixed to p=0, and use the setup
in the rain-example in 

http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials/spde-tutorial


where you have your own model for 'p'. if y>0, then you know that 'you
do not have y=0', which has prob 1-p, and you observe y ~ f(y|y>0). 


if you want the 'type1' version, then you cannot use this setup, as
observing y=0 you do not know which component it came from.

for continous response this is particular easy, as you can never
observe y==0  by chance.

let me know if you have further questions

H




--
Håvard Rue
